claims: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) is an independent U.S. government agency.
The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) was established in 1914.
The FTC regulates advertising.
The FTC regulates privacy.
The FTC regulates antitrust issues.
The FTC regulates fraud.
The FTC's mission is to protect consumers from fraud/deception and promote competition by enforcing antitrust laws.
The FTC is composed of five Commissioners.
FTC Commissioners are appointed by the President for 7-year terms.
No more than three FTC Commissioners are from the same political party.
The FTC has a Bureau of Consumer Protection.
The FTC's Bureau of Consumer Protection prevents fraudulent and deceptive practices.
The FTC has a Bureau of Competition.
The FTC's Bureau of Competition enforces antitrust laws to maintain competitive markets.
The FTC has a Bureau of Economics.
The FTC's Bureau of Economics analyzes the impact of FTC actions on the economy.
The FTC files lawsuits against companies.
The FTC issues regulations such as the Franchise Rule.
The FTC provides educational resources.
Consumers can report fraud, scams, or unfair business practices at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.
